key_insight: Negabytes: zero-capex, savings-shared reclaim targets the non-hyperscale fleets that never deployed TMO/zswap; pulling the freed DDR5 and reselling it at 4x prices makes savings metered and adds compatible supply.
killer_doubt: VMware's NVMe memory tiering went GA in VCF 9.0, June 2025 (via search snippet), inside existing licenses; below ~15% p99-safe reclaim, the savings share cannot cover service costs.
decisive_experiment: Three 90-day enterprise pilots (VMware, KVM, Kubernetes): DAMON/esxtop coldness profiling, then zswap/NVMe/CXL tiering under a p99 SLO guarantee. Measure GB freed, pull or swap DIMMs, and test a third-party M&V baseline. ~$300k.
prior_art: Energy ESCOs/IPMVP; Meta TMO (ASPLOS 2022); Google far memory (ASPLOS 2019); VMware VCF 9 tiering (via search snippet). Shared-savings memory contracts: none found.

key_insight: Pricing per effective GB shifts data-reduction risk to the vendor, as storage arrays did; fleets with identical weights and prompt prefixes are the one place 10x is plausible.
killer_doubt: Weights live in HBM; prefix sharing is already software (vLLM, Mooncake). Confidential VMs (SEV-SNP/TDX) hold ciphertext that neither compresses nor dedups, capping general workloads near 1.5-2x.
decisive_experiment: Snapshot host DRAM of 100 AI-inference nodes and 100 general cloud hosts; compute 64 B-line LZ4 ratio and cross-host 4 KB duplicate fraction, excluding encrypted VMs. Kill below 2x effective. ~$60k.
prior_art: Marvell Structera A inline-LZ4 CXL expander; ZeroPoint compression IP; IBM MXT; HICAMP dedup (ASPLOS 2012); storage effective-capacity pricing [training knowledge].

key_insight: OMI and FB-DIMM died of single-vendor lock-in; an open, generation-agnostic CXL Type-3 buffer with ECC and patrol scrub lets retired DIMMs serve new CPUs.
killer_doubt: Marvell Structera X already drives DDR4 behind CXL. DDR3's 4 Gb dies give ~16 GB per DIMM at ~2-3x DDR5 watts per GB, so the generation-agnostic part adds little.
decisive_experiment: Price a three-PHY versus DDR4-only controller (die area and NRE from a PHY IP quote) and count DDR3 versus DDR4 GB in 2026 ITAD lots. Drop DDR3 support if under 10% of reusable GB. ~$20k.
prior_art: IBM OMI / Microchip SMC 1000; FB-DIMM AMB; Marvell Structera X (DDR4/DDR5 CXL); Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Health telemetry plus hot-page migration toward the best devices could make a heterogeneous used-DIMM pool behave like one qualified capacity tier.
killer_doubt: Chipkill lockstep across mixed ranks runs at the slowest timing and breaks on mixed x4/x8 widths. Same lever as GreenSKU and Structera X; phone LPDDR harvest is I-06854.
decisive_experiment: FPGA CXL card with two DDR4 channels of deliberately mixed DIMMs (vendor, speed, x4/x8). Measure lockstep bandwidth loss, chipkill coverage and migration overhead on Redis/memcached traces. ~$150k.
prior_art: Marvell Structera X; Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Meta TPP page placement; study items I-00224 (HOLD) and I-06854 (ADVANCE).

key_insight: Retired DDR4 behind a CXL controller with symbol ECC is wafer-free capacity for DDR5-only CPUs: the plainest statement of the reuse lever.
killer_doubt: Already deployed (GreenSKU, Structera X). DDR4 prices jumped after 2025 end-of-life notices [training knowledge], so value capture, not technology, is open; ~$0.3-0.8/GB card cost per I-00224.
decisive_experiment: None separate: fold into the I-00224 pilot (1,000 retired RDIMMs retested, a commercial DDR4 CXL expander in a tier-2 cloud, landed $/GB and slowdown).
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; Meta and Google DDR4-via-CXL reuse (prior study search snippet).

key_insight: Inference fleets hold many identical bytes (weights, images, libraries); a rack-scale content-addressed CXL pool could keep one copy for 64-128 hosts.
killer_doubt: The 50-100x needs weights in host DRAM; they live in HBM. Mooncake/vLLM already share prefixes by hash in software, and dedup side channels killed cross-tenant KSM.
decisive_experiment: Same snapshot study as I-07802: hash 4 KB host-DRAM pages across 64 inference hosts and count duplicates not already shared by software. Kill below 1.3x. ~$50k.
prior_art: HICAMP (ASPLOS 2012); Linux KSM; Mooncake KV pool (FAST 2025); vLLM prefix caching; Flip Feng Shui dedup attack (USENIX Security 2016).

key_insight: Price signals could allocate pooled idle DRAM to the jobs that value it most, which matters more at 4x prices.
killer_doubt: Microsoft Pond measured ~7% savings from CXL pools. Reclaiming a 64 GB lease at ~10 GB/s takes ~6 s of migration, so per-millisecond leases are fiction.
decisive_experiment: Replay Azure and Alibaba VM traces in a pooling-plus-auction simulator with realistic migration bandwidth. Kill if GB recovered per rack at p99 SLO beats static pooling by under 5 points. ~$30k.
prior_art: Microsoft Pond (ASPLOS 2023); Memtrade harvested-memory marketplace (SIGMETRICS 2023); CXL pooling appliances (UnifabriX, XConn); study item I-04804 (DROP).

key_insight: Same reuse lever framed as cheap bridge cards for 8-16 RDIMMs; running old DIMMs slower cuts power and error rate, not wear.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-08711. DRAM barely wears out, so down-clocking buys little life; 16 RDIMMs draw ~65-95 W per card and need 4+ channels.
decisive_experiment: None separate: fold into the I-00224 pilot.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; Azure, Meta and Google DDR4-via-CXL reuse (prior study search snippet).

key_insight: Field studies show past corrected errors strongly predict future failures; a signed per-DIMM log carries that signal, which a short burn-in cannot, into resale of reclaimed DDR5.
killer_doubt: For DDR4 the binding barrier is DDR5-only sockets, not trust. Seller-signed logs need operator keys; if history beats a 1-hour test by under 2x at predicting failures, drop.
decisive_experiment: From one partner fleet, take 2,000 DIMMs with 3+ years of BMC error logs, burn-in test them, then run 6 months in a CXL tier. Compare history versus burn-in as predictors of second-life UEs. ~$150k.
prior_art: Schroeder et al., DRAM errors in the wild (SIGMETRICS 2009); EU Digital Product Passport (ESPR); DDR5 SPD end-user bytes [training knowledge]. DIMM passport: none found.

key_insight: Shredding policies, not physics, can pull reusable DIMMs out of supply; an auditable verification test lets disposal policies accept power removal.
killer_doubt: Vendor manuals citing NIST 800-88 already treat 5-10 min power removal as DRAM 'Clear' (via search snippet); cold-boot work measured seconds-to-minutes room-temperature remanence. Little left to change.
decisive_experiment: Survey 30 ITAD firms and 20 enterprise disposal policies for the fraction of retired DIMMs shredded; drop if under 10%. ~$30k. Remanence physics needs no new study.
prior_art: NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 (via vendor-manual search snippets); Halderman et al., cold-boot attacks (USENIX Security 2008); IEEE 2883-2022 sanitization standard.

key_insight: Grading retired DIMMs by retention and row-hammer threshold lets an exchange route weak parts to cold, single-tenant tiers and sell warranted capacity at ~20-30% of new.
killer_doubt: Hyperscalers reuse their own retirements (GreenSKU), leaving the exchange the leftovers; DDR4 prices rose after 2025 EOL notices [training knowledge], squeezing a ~20-30%-of-new price.
decisive_experiment: Grade 2,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs for retention at 45-85 C, row-hammer threshold (DRAM Bender-style FPGA) and speed bin. Report yield per grade, test cost per GB and landed $/GB in a CXL sled. ~$250k.
prior_art: ITRenew/Iron Mountain Sesame resale; Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024); Marvell Structera X; DRAM Bender/SoftMC testers; study item I-00224 (HOLD).

key_insight: DSA on sparse ArF guides can print sub-10 nm hex arrays with spin-and-bake tools, attacking EUV cost and U.S. chemistry supply at once.
killer_doubt: At 10 nm pitch the node is ~2-5 aF (~10-30 electrons at 1 V), readable only by a second gain transistor that breaks 4F2; DSA defectivity remains far above targets.
decisive_experiment: University nanofab: PS-PDMS DSA on ArF guide posts to 10-12 nm-pitch hex holes over 1 cm2; SEM placement error and missing/merged-hole density. Kill above 1 per cm2. ~$200k.
